questions.prompt: What does the Count property of a List<T> return?
questions.explanation: Count is the number of items actually in the list.

questions.prompt: Which statement creates an empty, type-safe list of integers?
questions.explanation: new List<int>() creates an empty generic list of ints.

questions.prompt: After adding items to a List, which statement is TRUE?
options: Count is the number stored; Capacity may be larger
questions.explanation: Capacity is the allocated room; Count is the items stored. Capacity >= Count.

questions.prompt: To look up a Dictionary value without risking an exception, use:
questions.explanation: TryGetValue returns true and sets the out value when the key exists.

questions.prompt: A List can hold duplicates and keeps them in ______ order.
questions.template: A List can hold duplicates and keeps them in ______ order.
questions.explanation: A List preserves the order in which items were added.

questions.prompt: Looking up a key that does not exist in a Dictionary throws:
questions.explanation: Reading a missing key throws KeyNotFoundException.

questions.prompt: To add an item at a specific position in a List, use:
questions.explanation: Insert(index, item) places an item at the given position.

questions.prompt: Which method removes the first occurrence of a value from a List<T>?
questions.explanation: Remove(x) removes the first match of x.
